result.note: Tests the August 2026 lifting of the wheat export ban: the ban timeline and record harvest, the notifying body, and the Black Sea disruption behind high prices.

questions.prompt: In August 2026, India lifted its ban on wheat exports. Consider the following statements about the ban and its background:
items: The ban on wheat exports was first imposed in May 2022.
The export curbs were extended to wheat flour in August 2022.
India's last wheat harvest before the lifting of the ban, at 120.6 million tonnes, fell short of the country's previous record.
questions.ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: The first two statements are correct. The third is wrong because the 120.6 million tonne harvest was an all-time high, rebuilding the buffer that the heatwave-hit 2022 crop had drained.
questions.source: India's last harvest hit an all-time high of 120.6 million tonnes, rebuilding the buffer the 2022 crop had drained.

questions.prompt: In August 2026, India scrapped its ban on exports of wheat, durum wheat, flour and related products. Which body issued the notifications clearing these shipments?
options: Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices
Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs
questions.explain: The DGFT notifications cleared shipments of wheat, the durum variety, flour and related products. The ban had been in place since May 2022, after a price spike following Russia's invasion of Ukraine pulled record volumes of Indian wheat abroad.
questions.source: clearing shipments of wheat, the durum variety, flour, and related products through notifications from the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT).

questions.prompt: In August 2026, attacks on commercial vessels and ports in which sea disrupted grain flows from major exporters and pushed Chicago wheat futures to a two-year high?
questions.explain: Escalating Russia-Ukraine attacks in the Black Sea disrupted grain flows from some of the world's top exporters. Indian shipments could ease pressure on import-dependent countries across Asia, Africa and West Asia.
questions.source: Escalating Russia-Ukraine attacks on commercial vessels and ports in the Black Sea have disrupted grain flows from some of the world's top exporters and pushed Chicago wheat futures to a two-year high.
